publications.summary: With an objective to enhancing transparency and providing greater clarity to the investors, Reserve Bank introduced the Benchmark Issuance Strategy (BIS) on a pilot basis commencing Q1: FY 2026-27 involving nine States, viz., Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Keralam, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh. Subsequently, nine other States and one Union Territory (UT), namely Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Manipur, Meghalaya, Odisha, Punjab, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Delhi were included under BIS framework from Q2: FY 2026-27 . Based on experience gained and concurrence received from six more States and one UT, the BIS framework is being extended to States of Assam, Goa, Haryana, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura and UT of Jammu and Kashmir, starting from Q3: FY 2026-27. publications.title: FINMA Executive Board: Alexandra Karg to leave FINMA; new division to be created
publications.summary: Alexandra Karg, Head of the Operations division and a member of the Executive Board, has decided to leave the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA on 30 November 2026, after 10 successful years. FINMA’s CEO and Executive Board thank Alexandra Karg for her valuable contribution during her time at FINMA. As a result of this departure, the organisational structure will also be adjusted. Specifically, the Operations division will be streamlined and renamed Digital and Infrastructure. A new division – Business Management and Strategy – will be established, comprising the Finance, Human Resources, Communications, CEO Office and Implementation of Transformation sections and groups, and will ensure integrated business management in line with the defined strategy.

publications.title: ESMA calls for changes to make MiCA clearer, safer and ready for emerging services
publications.summary: ESMA calls for changes to make MiCA clearer, safer and ready for emerging services 30 September 2026 Digital Finance and Innovation Investor protection Simplification and Burden Reduction The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has responded to the European Commission’s public consultation on the review of Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). ESMA’s recommendations aim to simplify the framework while improving investor protection and addressing innovative business models, such as decentralised finance (DeFi), staking, lending and borrowing.
